title: From RSD to Clusters: A Parameter-Locked Test of Late-Time Structure Growth
description: Propagates redshift-space distortion (RSD) constraints on the effective gravitational coupling into parameter-locked predictions for galaxy cluster abundances under Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC). With no parameters fit to cluster data and high-z (CMB) normalization, the paper predicts a +6.4% total cluster excess vs. ΛCDM and a distinctive negative tilt in the redshift-distribution shape ratio R(z), providing sealed, falsifiable targets for eRASS1.

effective_gravity.description: Effective gravitational coupling used in the growth equation for EFC; the amplitude \alpha_{L2}=0.34\pm0.16 is fixed by BOSS DR12 RSD.

shape_ratio.description: Redshift-distribution shape ratio comparing EFC to ΛCDM, used to isolate redshift-dependent growth signatures.

fractional_distribution.description: Definition of the fractional cluster redshift distribution within a survey sample; uniform multiplicative mass-calibration errors cancel to first order.

high_z_normalization.description: High-redshift (CMB-consistent) normalization used for the linear growth factor D(a), ensuring identical primordial initial conditions across models.

key_results.main_finding: With \alpha_{L2}=0.34 from BOSS DR12 RSD and high-z normalization, EFC predicts N_EFC/N_\LambdaCDM = 1.064 and a negative dR/dz shape tilt (∼+5% at z≈0.15 to ∼−6% at z≈0.7) for eRASS1-like cluster samples, without fitting any parameters to cluster data.
datasets_used: Planck-consistent cosmological parameters (for P(k) via CLASS)

sealed_predictions.statement: Total abundance enhancement N_EFC / N_\LambdaCDM = 1.064 ± 0.02 for M > 10^{14} M_\odot and 0.1 < z < 0.8 under CMB-consistent normalization.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: eRASS1 total cluster counts after weak-lensing mass calibration (DES Y3/KiDS-1000/HSC).

sealed_predictions.statement: Negative redshift-gradient in the shape ratio: R(z) transitions from ≈1.05 at z≈0.15 to ≈0.94 at z≈0.7 (dR/dz < 0), robust to uniform mass-calibration errors.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Binned redshift-distribution shape test using eRASS1 clusters with uniform mass calibration.

sealed_predictions.statement: Crossover near z ≈ 0.3–0.4 where R(z) ≈ 1, separating low-z excess from high-z deficit.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Detection (or lack) of the R(z) ≈ 1 crossing in eRASS1 redshift-binned counts.
Comparison of measured binned redshift fractions to the sealed bin-by-bin predictions using eRASS1.

kill_criteria: KC1: Observed total eRASS1 cluster abundance (after mass calibration) is less than or equal to ΛCDM predictions, contradicting the predicted +5–8% excess.
KC2: The measured shape ratio R(z) exhibits a positive gradient dR/dz ≥ 0 or is consistent with a flat trend at the ≤1% level across 0.1 < z < 0.8.
KC3: No observed crossover near z ≈ 0.3–0.4 where R(z) ≈ 1, contrary to the predicted tilt pattern.

KC4: Strong inconsistency between independent RSD constraints and the required growth enhancement (e.g., updated RSD rejecting \alpha_{L2} ≈ 0.34 within stated uncertainty), breaking the parameter lock.
abstract: A cross-probe test of late-time structure growth propagating RSD constraints on effective gravitational coupling into galaxy cluster abundance predictions with zero free parameters fit to cluster data.

methodology.inference_chain: RSD → Growth history D(z) → Mass function → Cluster counts
methodology.key_feature: No parameters fit to cluster data

shape_observable.definition: R(z) = R_EFC(z) / R_ΛCDM(z), where R(z) = N(z)/N_total
shape_observable.advantage: Robust against uniform multiplicative mass-calibration errors

falsified_if: Fewer total clusters than ΛCDM (after mass calibration)
Positive dR/dz (more high-z fraction than low-z)

data_context.mass_calibration: DES Y3, KiDS-1000, HSC weak lensing

normalization.rationale: Forward prediction from CMB, not retrodiction

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first parameter-locked cross-probe prediction chain in EFC: RSD → growth → clusters, with zero free parameters fit to cluster data. It deposits four quantitative sealed predictions (total abundance excess, shape-ratio tilt, crossover redshift, per-bin R(z)) that are directly falsifiable by eRASS1 cluster catalogues. It does not close any existing KC or theory gap but opens a new high-value falsification surface and strengthens EFC's claim to be a genuinely predictive framework rather than a post-hoc fitting exercise.
graph_insights: No existing graph nodes were found within 2 hops, indicating this paper opens an entirely new observational branch (galaxy clusters / halo mass function) in the EFC knowledge graph — it should seed new concept nodes for 'shape ratio R(z)', 'parameter-locked prediction', 'cross-probe chain', and 'eRASS1 cluster validation', all connected to the existing 'redshift-space distortions' and 'BOSS DR12' nodes.

The absence of related validation tests in the graph means the 5 new planned-pipeline tests above represent net-new coverage; test count should move from 119 total to 124, with pipeline count from 18 to 23.

The concept 'cross-probe test' touched by this paper is structurally significant: it is the first graph edge connecting the RSD/growth observable family to the cluster-count observable family, creating a bridge that will propagate constraints (or kills) bidirectionally when either data source updates.

implicit_consequences: The shape-ratio tilt dR/dz < 0 is a smoking-gun signature that cannot be mimicked by uniform mass-calibration bias, giving EFC a systematics-robust discriminant against LCDM — this implicitly raises the evidential weight of cluster tests relative to total-count tests.

If DESI DR2 RSD data shift alpha_L2 significantly away from 0.34, the entire cluster prediction chain collapses simultaneously (paper KC4), creating a correlated kill channel between the DESI rapid-response pipeline (existing biggest gap) and this new cluster test — the two are now logically entangled.

The paper implicitly constrains the EFC transition function f_transition(a) shape: the crossover at z≈0.3–0.4 means any future theoretical refinement of the transition scale (e.g., from ADM Hamiltonian analysis, theory-adm-hamiltonian-stability) must preserve activation below z~0.5 or the cluster predictions are invalidated.

Using the Tinker HMF calibrated in LCDM N-body simulations is an explicit approximation noted in the paper — this creates a theory gap for EFC-specific N-body halo-finding that, if pursued, could shift the central prediction; future simulations addressing theory-adm-hamiltonian-stability could feed back here.

The sealed per-bin predictions (P4) at Δz=0.1 resolution effectively provide a 6-point template that can be cross-correlated with weak-lensing mass calibration bins, implicitly linking this test to future Euclid/Rubin cluster weak-lensing analyses.

The f·sigma8(z=0.7) sealed prediction (action-5 / DESI pipeline) and the cluster R(z≈0.7)≈0.94 prediction are now two independent observables probing the same underlying growth enhancement at the same redshift — a joint pass or joint fail would be highly constraining.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_change: Biggest gap remains DESI DR2 full-shape RSD rapid-response pipeline, but add secondary urgency note: eRASS1 mass-calibrated cluster catalogue validation pipeline also needed — the two are now correlated via alpha_L2 parameter lock, and a joint verification script covering both the fsigma8 sealed prediction and the cluster shape-ratio predictions would maximise EFC's falsification surface when either dataset drops.
